title: Add the auditor role and fix the stale max_concurrency test
summary: Retry the rejected auditor job: add an auditor role (fixed prompt, typed finding output, core module, `athena audit` command), judged against BRIEF.md and owner goals. Also fix the base-failing drain test `a_change_to_max_concurrency_alone_does_not_invalidate_a_reading`, which blocked the last attempt. The check-attribution machinery from the introspection is left out as a separate request. The audience is the owner.

defaults_applied.how: New auditor tests; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
The check-attribution work is split off; only the auditor and the one blocking test are changed.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt and the audit command.
Criteria check a recorded finding and the rejection of a finding with no evidence, not that files exist.
The prompt protection is marked prose-only.
The stale test fixture is fixed so the test follows the config's value.
Docs and the changelog are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience is the owner, who wants a grader whose yardstick jobs cannot change.

The failing test is stale, not a product bug: athena.toml now has `max_concurrency = 1`, but the test (drain.rs ~1102) replaces `max_concurrency = 2`, so `before` and `after` are equal and assert_ne! fails. This was read from the repository, not run.
The fix is to the test: replace `max_concurrency = 1` with 2 and 3. athena.toml is not changed.

The introspection's proposed baseline-vs-change check attribution is a separate, larger request. Only the typed request (retry the auditor job) plus the one blocking test is done, per the small default.
The first attempt's deliverable list is reused, plus crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked`. All tests pass, including `a_change_to_max_concurrency_alone_does_not_invalidate_a_reading`, and new tests that run the auditor against a fake driver and check it records a typed finding.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

In drain.rs the max_concurrency test builds `before` and `after` from the config's actual `max_concurrency = 1` value, so the two differ and the test still asserts that the reading is not invalidated. athena.toml is unchanged.

roles.rs defines an auditor role with a fixed prompt constant and a valid RoleDefinition. The prompt says to judge outcomes against BRIEF.md and the owner's goals rather than a job's own criteria, to look at real outcomes rather than records, and to cite evidence for each finding.
Run `cargo test`. A test shows the auditor's brief contains BRIEF.md and not the job's acceptance criteria. Another shows a finding with no evidence is rejected.
Run `cargo run -- audit --help`, or the equivalent test. The command exists and, with the fake driver, produces a recorded auditor invocation visible to the owner in CLI output.
Role::Auditor round-trips through the parse and as_str functions in records.rs, and every exhaustive match on Role compiles.
No warden code is added. BRIEF.md, athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflow files are not edited. CHANGELOG.md has an auditor entry.
The docs or code comments state that the auditor's prompt is protected from jobs only by being a fixed constant, that the warden request will enforce this, and that this is prose-only.

out_of_scope: Baseline-versus-change check attribution and per-criterion verdicts when a check fails (a separate request).
Edits to BRIEF.md, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
departures: The change is larger than a typical job: it touches many crates, and the first attempt failed. That raises cost and time above the reference.
